items.item: The grid header names the week with its date range (such as "Week 45 · 2–8 Nov 2026"), every day column shows the weekday and date, and controls move to the previous, next and current week
items.evidence: el.rangeHeading shows '02/11/2026 – 08/11/2026' (updateRangeHeading()); each <th> in renderGridHead() renders WEEKDAY_SHORT[d] + fmtDate(date) e.g. 'T2 · 02/11/2026'; #btnToday, #btnPrevWeek ('‹'), #btnNextWeek ('›') all wired to shift state.weekStart.

items.item: Each shift shows its start and end time in one consistent 24-hour format and the role or station (such as "07:00–15:00 · Cashier"), and a shift that ends after midnight is marked as ending the next day
items.evidence: shiftCellHtml() renders shift-type label (e.g. 'Ca sáng') on one line and '06:00–14:00' on a second line — never 'time · role/station' in one line, and role/department is only shown once per employee row, not per shift. The night shift (SHIFT_TYPES.night: start 22:00, end 06:00) is rendered as plain '22:00–06:00' with no next-day indicator anywhere in shiftCellHtml() or its aria-label.

items.item: Each staff row shows the week's scheduled hours against contracted hours (such as "36 / 40 h"), the scheduled figure equals that person's shifts less unpaid breaks, and anyone over or under contract is flagged in words
items.evidence: EMPLOYEES objects (id, name, role, dept, code, initials, color) carry no contracted-hours field, and no row in renderGridBody()/identity markup displays any hours total or over/under-contract flag.

items.item: A footer row shows, for each day, the staff count or hours scheduled against the required cover, and days below the requirement are marked in text (such as "Short 1")
items.evidence: renderGridFoot(): <tfoot> row 'Đã xếp ca / Tổng NV' shows e.g. '7/8', and when scheduled < total*MIN_COVERAGE_RATIO it adds amber text 'Thiếu nhân sự' (visible on CN column '4/8 · Thiếu nhân sự' in screenshot).

items.item: The sample data contains at least one rule conflict, such as overlapping shifts for one person or less than 11 hours' rest between a closing and the next opening shift, shown on the affected cell with a written reason
items.evidence: BASE_TYPE data has instances of <11h rest (e.g. e3 afternoon 14:00–22:00 Thu then morning 06:00–14:00 Fri = 8h rest) but there is no conflict-detection code anywhere in the script, no cell styling/badge for conflicts, and no written reason is ever rendered.

items.item: Approved leave, days off and public holidays appear as labelled cells (such as "Annual leave", "Day off") that look different from an empty, unscheduled cell
items.evidence: SHIFT_TYPES only defines morning/afternoon/night/off ('Nghỉ'); 'Nghỉ' is visually distinct from the dashed '+ Thêm ca' empty cell, but there is no separate 'Annual leave' or 'public holiday' category anywhere in SHIFT_TYPES, BASE_TYPE, or the legend — only a single generic day-off type exists.

items.item: The week's status (Draft or Published) is shown, and publishing goes through a confirmation that names the week and the number of unresolved conflicts or warnings
items.evidence: Per-shift draft/published state surfaces via draftBanner text ('Có 16 ca chưa công bố...') and list-view badges, but there is no single week-level Draft/Published status label. el.btnPublish's click handler calls publishWeek(key) and shows a toast directly — openConfirm() is never invoked for publishing, so there is no confirmation dialog at all, let alone one naming the week or conflict count.

items.item: The grid is a <table> with staff names as row headers and days as column headers, and each shift or empty cell is keyboard-reachable with an accessible name that includes the person and the date (such as "Add shift, Lan Pham, Tue 3 Nov")
items.evidence: <table id="rosterTable">; renderGridBody() emits '<th scope="row">' per employee name; renderGridHead() emits '<th scope="col">' per day. shiftCellHtml() buttons carry aria-label e.g. 'Nguyễn Thị Lan, chưa xếp ca, Thứ Hai 02/11/2026. Nhấn để thêm ca.' and arrow-key navigation is wired via rosterTbody keydown handler.

items.item: A week with no shifts yet shows a message with a way to start (such as "Copy last week"), and a loading state and a load error with a retry button exist
items.evidence: renderEmptyWeek() shows 'Chưa có lịch cho tuần này' plus a button labelled 'Sao chép lịch tuần trước' or 'Bắt đầu xếp lịch' (reachable via ?state=empty); renderSkeleton() provides pulsing skeleton rows (?state=loading); renderError() shows 'Không thể tải lịch phân ca' with a '#btnRetryLoad Thử lại' retry button (?state=error).

notes: Page is in Vietnamese (lang="vi"); checklist examples translated conceptually. No stylistic template tells were found — no gradients, glass, uppercase tracked labels, emoji icons, KPI tiles, promo cards, or oversized radii (radii are 4–6px per audit.json). Shift-type color coding (blue/amber/violet) is functional and has an explicit legend, not a gratuitous rainbow-status pattern. Main gaps are functional: no per-shift role/station + midnight-crossing marker, no contracted-hours tracking, no conflict detection, no leave/holiday cell types, and no publish confirmation dialog despite the UI otherwise using openConfirm() for the destructive delete-shift and copy-week-overwrite actions.
